sentences.text:
Prakash Rathor vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 January,
2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:5594
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Sandeep N. Bhatt
 On The 20th Of January, 2026

Writ Petition No. 13653 of 2012
 Prakash Rathor And Others
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Abhishek Arjaria - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri Tapan Bathre - Panel Lawyer for the State.

Order 
The present petition is filed praying the following reliefs:
"(i) To allow the petition by setting aside the order dated 26/05/2012 (Annex.P-5)
passed by the Adjudicating Officer and consequently petitioners be acquitted.
(ii) Any other order/orders, writ or writs may kindly be passed bythis Hon'ble Court along with the cost of this petition."

On 03.04.2013, this Court passed the following order:
"Shri Abhishek Arjariya, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri P. K. Kourav, learned Additional Advocate General with Shri Rajesh Tiwari, learned Govt. Adv. for the respondents.

On 25.9.2012 this Court had directed the respondents to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:5594 2 WP-13653-2012 constitute the Tribunals and Special Courts as required under Section 70 and 74 of the Food Safety Act but till date nothing has been done.
Shri Kourav prays for a week's time to seek instructions in the matter.

sentences.text: It is seen that under the Food Safety Act action is taken and the Food item and vehicle used on certain occasion are seized and applications are filed for seeking release of the vehicle or the seized item on Supurtagi.

The specified authority in various cases expressed their inability to release the vehicle on the ground that they do not have such a power under the statute and when the application is filed before the Chief Judicial Magistrate or the Magistrate concerned they are also not interfering as there is no Court specified or constituted, for dealing with the case.
The aggrieved persons are left remedyless in the matter .

Shri Kourav is directed to seek instructions and intimate to this Court as to what steps are being taken by the State Government for ensuring that proper remedies are available to the aggrieved persons for seeking enforcement of their right"

Today when the matter is taken up, learned counsel for the parties jointly submitted that now the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal as required under Sections 70 and 74 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is notified and the concerned Sessions Court in each district is notified as the appellate tribunal.

Therefore, the matter is required to be referred to the Sessions Court, Bhopal constituted as Food Safety Appellate Tribunal under NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:5594 3 WP-13653-2012 Sections 70-74 of the Act of 2006.
In view, the matter is referred to the aforesaid Food Safety Appellate Tribunal at Bhopal.

entities.text: Food Safety Appellate Tribunal at Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is expected that since the matter is pending since 2012, the same shall be decided by the aforesaid Tribunal expeditiously in accordance with law.
As the interim order is already in favour of the petitioners, it is directed that the interim order passed by this Court shall be operative until further order passed by the appellate tribunal.
Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT) JUDGE ks Prakash Rathor vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46377718/
